what: Margin rubric. What a correct answer to one lesson question needs and what each score means, written by Margin on a teacher's key. Keyed by a fingerprint of the question; no question text, no student work, no names.

rubric.asks: What the farming systems suggest about Tiwanaku society, plus a supporting reason
rubric.note: Students watch the video first, but this is their own observation, so any reasonable reading of the fields counts.

bands.means: Says something about what their society was like, and points to something in the fields or canals as the reason.
Says something about what their society was like, but gives no reason from the fields or canals.
Describes the raised fields or canals only, without saying what that shows about the people.
Mentions the Tiwanaku, farming, or the video without answering the question. Worth 1 point.

examples.answer: I think they were organized and worked together, because building all those canals and raised fields would take a lot of people planning it out.
It shows their society was smart and advanced.
They made raised fields with water canals in between them so the crops stayed warmer.
The Tiwanaku lived near Lake Titicaca in Bolivia.
